text:
Noah R: Quick sync  we keep getting product questions about why console shows red but API returns 200 in some fallback cases.
Priya S: Is this the alt-model fallback case? We routed to smaller model and returned 200 w/ note, console still flagged red and gave upgrade CTA.
Noah R: Yup. That mismatch triggers support tickets. Also billing thinks a 200 = success and doesn't mark fallback usage differently.
Alex D: We need a small spec: canonical surface for any runtime decision that affects user expectations: (1) server_tag, (2) client_code, (3) http_status, (4) console_badge, (5) sla_counting.
Tasha L: + telemetry fields and a concise help copy. Ops wants to alert when fallback >3% in 1m.
Priya S: Proposed enums: server_tag in [OK, DEGRADED, THROTTLED, QUOTA_BLOCKED, FAIL]. client_code strings: ROUTE_DEGRADED, QUEUE_THROTTLED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, INTERNAL_ERROR. HTTP mapping: DEGRADED -> 200, THROTTLED -> 429, QUOTA_BLOCKED -> 429, FAIL -> 503.
Noah R: Important: SDKs must surface ROUTE_DEGRADED as a warning payload even when HTTP 200. Otherwise callers can't adapt.
Alex D: Agree. Implementation detail: add headers: `X-Redwood-Server-Tag`, `X-Redwood-Client-Code`, and `X-Redwood-Retry-After` (if applicable).
Priya S: Telemetry fields: `telemetry.route_reason`, `telemetry.fallback_model`, `telemetry.quota_bucket`, `telemetry.retry_after_secs`, `telemetry.user_visible_flag` (bool). Also emit `metric.success_but_degraded`.
Tasha L: Console mapping: OK->green (no CTA), DEGRADED->amber (tooltip: short copy + "Why?" link), THROTTLED/QUOTA_BLOCKED->red (CTA: upgrade docs + backoff tips), FAIL->red with incident banner.
Noah R: SLA counting: default behavior is count HTTP 200 as success for uptime, but we must tag `success_but_degraded` and not count degraded completions toward model-accuracy SLAs. Product requested a toggle to treat degraded as failure for strict customers.
Alex D: SDK behavior:
- If HTTP != 2xx -> return structured error envelope with client_code, message, retry_after
- If HTTP == 2xx and client_code == ROUTE_DEGRADED -> surface a Warning object and expose `degraded=true` in response struct
Example warning envelope to return in SDK docs:
```json
{
  "client_code": "ROUTE_DEGRADED",
  "message": "request served by lower-latency model (gpt-lite-1), results may differ",
  "fallback_model": "gpt-lite-1"
}
```
Priya S: For server-side backwards compatibility: keep 200 for graceful degrade (so older clients keep working) but add the headers so newer SDKs pick it up.
Tasha L: Ops: set an alert when `metric.fallback_rate` > 3% (1m window) and when `metric.quota_denied_rate` > 0.5% for paid customers.
Noah R: Copy suggestions: DEGRADED tooltip (short): "We routed this request to a lower-cost model to preserve latency. Learn more." Quota CTA: "Youxceeded your quota. Upgrade or wait {retry_after}s."
Alex D: Edge case: we also have internal 409 queue_full -> map to client_code=QUEUE_THROTTLED + HTTP 429 so clients can backoff consistently.
Priya S: Decision checklist:
- add headers: X-Redwood-Server-Tag, X-Redwood-Client-Code, X-Redwood-Retry-After (Alex)
- SDK: surface degraded as Warning and add example enveloped responses (Noah)
- Telemetry: add fields & alerts (Tasha)
- Console: badge + CTA + tooltip update (Priya)
Ops-bot: rollout-sanity: feature-flag `status_surface_v1` present in runtime config.
Noah R: Timeline: implement headers + metric today, SDK PR targeting backward-compatible change tomorrow, console copy by EOD. Flip feature flag next Wednesday after smoke tests.
Priya S: I'll draft the tiny RFC with the enum table and curl examples to avoid ambiguity.
Tasha L: Will add alert runbook entries for the new metrics.
Noah R: Thanks all. If anyone hits an ambiguous mapping while implementing ping this thread with examples (response body + headers).
